question: A 40-year-old male visits a urologist and reports that for the past 2 weeks, his penis has been gradually curving to the right with associated pain during intercourse. He is able to have a normal erection and he does not recollect of any trauma to his penis. Although he is married, he admits to having unprotected sexual relationship with several females in the past year. His vitals are normal and physical examination in unremarkable except for a lesionless curved penis. It is painless to touch. Test results for sexually transmitted disease is pending. Which of the following is the most likely cause?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Curved penis" -> "possible Peyronie's disease" -> "fibrosis of tunica albuginea" -> "pain during intercourse" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Curved penis" -> "no recollection of trauma" -> "unlikely congenital hypospadias" -> "normal physical examination" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Curved penis" -> "unprotected sexual relationships" -> "possible sexually transmitted infection" -> "pending test results" -> "unclear cause" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Curved penis" -> "painless to touch" -> "suggests fibrosis rather than infection" -> "fibrosis of tunica albuginea" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Curved penis" -> "gradual onset over 2 weeks" -> "suggests chronic condition" -> "fibrosis of corpus cavernosa" -> "less likely than tunica albuginea" -> 75%
enhanced_information: The patient's symptoms of a gradually curving penis with associated pain during intercourse, alongside a normal physical examination and no recollection of trauma, suggest a diagnosis of Peyronie's disease, which is characterized by fibrosis of the tunica albuginea. The pain during intercourse aligns with the presence of fibrosis, as it can lead to discomfort. The gradual onset over 2 weeks indicates a chronic condition rather than an acute one, further supporting the likelihood of Peyronie's disease. Congenital hypospadias is unlikely due to the normal examination findings and lack of trauma history. While sexually transmitted infections could be a concern given the patient's history, the painless nature of the curvature and the absence of lesions make this less likely. Therefore, the most likely cause is fibrosis of the tunica albuginea, consistent with the consensus on Peyronie's disease.
analysis: The patient's symptoms of a gradually curving penis with associated pain during intercourse, along with a normal physical examination and no recollection of trauma, strongly suggest Peyronie's disease. This condition is characterized by the development of fibrous scar tissue in the tunica albuginea, leading to curvature and pain. The painless nature of the curvature and the absence of lesions further support this diagnosis, making sexually transmitted infections less likely. Congenital hypospadias is also unlikely due to the normal examination findings. Therefore, the most likely cause of the patient's symptoms is fibrosis of the tunica albuginea, consistent with the consensus on Peyronie's disease.
